li.p: Explain why \mathbb{P}_{n} is closed under the operation of usual polynomial addition. That is, explain why {\pvec}+ \qvec \in \mathbb{P}_{n} if \pvec, \qvec \in \mathbb{P}_{n}.
Explain why \mathbb{P}_{n} is closed under scalar multiplication. That is, explain why c{\pvec}\in \mathbb{P}_{n} if c \in \mathbb{R} and \pvec\in \mathbb{P}_{n}.
Identify/describe the zero element {\zerovec}\in \mathbb{P}_{n} in axiom (A3). Then show that \pvec +{\zerovec}= \pvec for every \pvec \in \mathbb{P}_{n}.
For an element \pvec \in \mathbb{P}_{n}, identify/describe the additive inverse -\pvec in axiom A4.
For elements \pvec, \qvec \in \mathbb{P}_{n}, show that axiom (SM1) holds.
If \pvec, \qvec \in \mathbb{P}_{n}, then both \pvec and \qvec are polynomials of degree at most n. Adding two such polynomials yields a polynomial \pvec + \qvec having degree at most n as well.

If \pvec\in \mathbb{P}_{n}, then \pvec(x)=a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n}. For any constant c, we then have (c\pvec)(x) \amp = c(a_{0}+a_{1}x+a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n}) \amp = c\cdot a_{0} + (c\cdot a_{1})x + (c \cdot a_{2})x^{2} + \ldots + (c \cdot a_{n})x^{n} which is clearly also in \mathbb{P}_{n}.

{\zerovec}(x) = 0 + 0x + 0x^{2} + \ldots 0x^{n}. If \pvec is any element in \mathbb{P}_{n}, then \pvec(x) = a_{0} + a_{1}x + a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n} so that \pvec(x) +{\zerovec}(x) \amp = (a_{0} + a_{1}x + a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n}) + (0 + 0x + 0x^{2} + \ldots 0x^{n}) \amp = (a_{0}+0) + (a_{1}+0)x + (a_{2}+0)x^{2} + \ldots + (a_{n}+0)x^{n} \amp = a_{0} + a_{1}x + a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n} \amp = \pvec(x).

If \pvec is any element in \mathbb{P}_{n}, then \pvec(x) = a_{0} + a_{1}x + a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n} and the additive inverse is -\pvec defined by -\pvec(x) = -a_{0} -a_{1}x - a_{2}x^{2} - \ldots - a_{n}x^{n}.

If \pvec is any element in \mathbb{P}_{n}, then \pvec(x) = a_{0} + a_{1}x + a_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + a_{n}x^{n}. Similarly, if \qvec is any element in \mathbb{P}_{n}, then \qvec(x) = b_{0} + b_{1}x + b_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + b_{n}x^{n}. For any constant k \in \mathbb{R}, we then have (k(\pvec+\qvec))(x) \amp = k(\pvec(x) + \qvec(x)) \amp = k((a_{0}+b_{0}) + (a_{1}+b_{1})x + (a_{2}+b_{2})x^{2} + \ldots + (a_{n}+b_{n})x^{n} \amp = ka_{0} + kb_{0} + ka_{1}x + kb_{1}x + ka_{2}x^{2} + kb_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + ka_{n}x^{n} + kb_{n}x^{n} \amp = (ka_{0} + ka_{1}x + ka_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + ka_{n}x^{n}) + (kb_{0} + kb_{1}x + kb_{2}x^{2} + \ldots + kb_{n}x^{n}) \amp = (k\pvec)(x) + (k\qvec)(x).
